Subject: Interest in annual commit tiers and smoothing options

Aditya,

Thanks for the product overview last week — PixelPay's payments team is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. We're evaluating a hosted API commit to replace some in-house generation for receipts and fraud scoring. Two quick asks from procurement before we schedule legal:  

- Can you send a concise annual commit matrix (Starter/Growth/Enterprise) with per-token pricing and clear overage rules? Our rough usage profile is ~150M tokens/month to start, with headroom to 400M/month in Q1.
- We need a billing smoothing option: monthly spend smoothing (so invoices don't spike) and a simple credit mechanism for initial onboarding over-usage.

Also share any standard fallback policies (e.g., model variant downgrade) for when peak capacity is constrained — that matters to our SREs. I'm attaching a short PDF that lists our procurement/contract checklist.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can we get a matrix by EOD Tuesday your time?

Best,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform Engineering, PixelPay

Subject: Re: Interest in annual commit tiers and smoothing options

Samir — thanks for the clarity and the checklist. Attach is a single-sheet commit matrix (CSV/XLSX) and a short FAQ. Highlights below so your procurement team can skim:  

Commit tiers (annual, prepaid commitment) — core proposal
- Starter: 12M tokens / year (~1M/mo equivalent) — $0.020 / 1k tokens
- Growth: 150M tokens / year (~12.5M/mo) — $0.011 / 1k tokens (15% off list)
- Enterprise: 1.5B tokens / year (~125M/mo) — $0.0065 / 1k tokens (45% off list)

Smoothing & Billing mechanics
- Monthly invoices against the annual committed token bank; unused tokens roll forward up to a 15% carry-forward cap for the year (not cumulative beyond term).
- Overages billed monthly at the per-token overage rate tied to the tier (Growth + 10% uplift).
- Onboarding safety credits: one-time credit can be applied for the first 30 days (we typically offer a small onboarding pool for large Growth/Enterprise deals).

Capacity fallback policy
- We support automated model downgrade to a compatible lower-cost variant (same API surface) with notification headers. For Enterprise, we include guaranteed throughput SLAs and regional failover lanes.

Next steps
- If you want, we can set a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow to align on numbers and procurement ask points. I've looped Neha (security/compliance touch) for any SOC 2 / data handling questions.

Attachments: 20261123_commit_matrix_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Forwarding Samir's ask and the matrix I sent. PixelPay is at ~150M/mo baseline right now but expects ramp to ~400M/mo. Key discussion points:  

- They asked specifically for smoothing and an onboarding credit. I proposed 15% carry-forward cap and a one-time onboarding credit for Growth/Enterprise.
- Pricing ladder I proposed: Starter / Growth / Enterprise (listed in attached matrix).

Two items I need help on:  
1) Approve a discretionary 10% additional discount on Enterprise if they commit 2B+ tokens AND sign a 24-month term (this is outside standard grid).
2) Confirm whether we can make the onboarding credit a non-recurring credit that doesn't affect ARR recognition (finance question for Marissa).

Notes from quick scan (Neha) on compliance: SOC 2 and regional failover are available but customer requested the specific evidence ASAP.

Aditya — thanks for the clear matrix. PixelPay is comfortable moving forward on the Growth tier (150M/year) subject to two items:

1) Billing smoothing: we need monthly smoothing such that our monthly invoices reflect even burn with token draw from the committed bank (your carry-forward approach sounds fine).
2) Onboarding safety pool: can Redwood provide a one-time onboarding credit (we estimate up to 10% overage in month 1 as we shift traffic) and confirm it won't be treated as a recurring discount.

If those are in writing, procurement will route paperwork to legal. Also please include the term length options (12 vs 24 months) and any volume break incentives at 24 months.

I've attached procurement contacts for our side.

Samir

Samir — great to see this moving forward. Confirming the terms we can commit to in writing:  

- Tier: Growth — 150M tokens / year, billed monthly against the committed bank.
- Term options: 12 months (standard) or 24 months (extra 6% lifetime discount on top of the Growth rate if they sign 24 months).
- Billing smoothing: Monthly invoices draw from the committed bank; unused tokens roll forward up to 15% of annual commitment.
- Overages: Billed at Growth overage rate (Growth per-token + 10% uplift).
- Onboarding safety pool: one-time credit equal to up to 10% of the first-month expected burn. This is a non-recurring credit and will be applied as a contra-revenue credit at invoice reconciliation (does not change the committed token bank).
- Optional: If PixelPay upgrades to Enterprise (>= 1.5B/yr) and signs 24 months, we can consider an additional 10% discretionary rebate to be structured as post-usage credits tied to attainment (subject to RevOps approval).

Next steps: I'll send a short commercial term sheet + DocuSign envelope today for the Growth 12-month option and route the 24-month incentive through Karthik/Marissa for approval if they ask. Linking the DocuSign here once I create the envelope.

Thanks — excited to get PixelPay onboarded.

--
